a, Detailed device schematic. A niobium film is patterned on a 500 μm thick 171Yb3+:YVO4 crystal. A 100 nm gold layer is evaporated on the back side, forming a weak optical Fabry-Pérot mode between the front and back chip reflections. b, Calibration of spin-cavity coupling strength. By optically pumping the population into the \(| \downarrow \rangle \) state, we probe the resonant spin-cavity coupling spectrum and its strength while avoiding superradiant effects. The blue data in the bottom subpanel correspond to the continuous-wave (CW) pump being off, while the black data are taken with a 400 μW continuous-wave pump. By fitting to a spin-cavity coupling model, we extract an ensemble coupling strength of \(\sqrt{N}g\approx 2\pi \times 1.1\) MHz, corresponding to a normalized coupling gnorm ≈ 0.6 < 1. The single-spin coupling, g = 2π × 10 Hz, and the effective ensemble size, N = 1010, are estimated from Comsol simulation and dopant concentration. c, Ensemble coupling strength, \(\sqrt{N}g\), as a function of pump power. We observe that the ensemble coupling strength increases with pump power, indicating a larger population in the microwave spin manifold.

Industry observers note that a, A pulsed, transient optical pumping scheme that drives 171Yb3+ spins into the \(| \uparrow \rangle \) state. The resulting inverted spin polarization is resonantly coupled to a microwave cavity, leading to a superradiant burst in the microwave domain. b, Example of a delayed superradiant burst. A 1 mW pump is applied for 50 μs, after which a microwave superradiant burst is observed with a delay time τd. The superradiant signal is normalized by its peak-to-peak amplitude. c and d, Burst delay times, τd, and burst width, τw, measured as a function of the optical pump detuning, Δpump, which controls the optical transition strength from \(| g\rangle \) to \(| \uparrow \rangle \). A symmetric dependence of τd and τw is observed, with shorter delay times and narrower widths near resonance. This behaviour is consistent with the expected scaling τd, τw ∝ 1/N, as the pump detuning effectively controls the ensemble size, N, in the microwave spin manifold. Data points represent mean values, with error bars indicating the standard deviation over 300 repeated measurements.

It has been revealed that a, Frequency-domain measurement of continuous-wave microwave superradiance, showing a much narrow linewidth of  ≈ 30 Hz. The inhomogeneously broadened ensemble line profile (dashed line) is overlaid for comparison. b, Dependence of the linewidth of continuous-wave superradiance on emission power, PMW. An inverse relationship between the linewidth and the emission power is observed, consistent with a noise-broadened Schawlow-Townes linewidth. The lower dashed line denotes the pump laser noise-limited bound. These results confirm that the disordered spin ensemble emits continuous-wave superradiance with a much narrower spectral linewidth. c, Continuous-wave superradiance emission frequency at different optical pump detunings. A linear correlation between the microwave emission frequency and optical pump detuning is observed, with a slope of  −1.23 kHz/MHz.

a, Four representative data traces under a 1 ms continuous optical pump. Random onset times of the emergent periodic pulsed phase are observed. b, Zoom-in of individual burst trains showing the distribution of burst onset times, {τk}, where k denotes the experimental repetition index. After an initial settling time, both the amplitudes, {Ak}, and the periodicity, T, become independent of k, indicating the establishment of a robust pulsed superradiance phase. c, Burst onset phases, defined as θk = 2π × τk/T (mod 2π), measured over 50 repetitions under identical experimental conditions. The phases are randomly distributed over 2π, demonstrating spontaneous breaking of continuous time-translation symmetry in the absence of any external timing reference.

a, Schematic of periodic pulsed superradiance, characterized by three parameters: the pulse-train periodicity T, the peak emission power Ppeak, and the average emission power \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\). b-d, show fits to the experimental data presented in Fig. 3 of the main text, where T, Ppeak, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\) exhibit good agreement with the expected scaling behaviours of T ∝ 1/N, Ppeak ∝ N2, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\propto {N}^{2}\), respectively. Here, N is the effective number of spins in the microwave manifold, tuned via the optical pump detuning, Δpump. When sweeping Δpump, the optical pump power is fixed, corresponding to an excitation over an optical inhomogeneity Γop = 2π × 92 MHz in all three cases.

a, Relative contributions of superradiance (blue) and stimulated emission (red) to the emission strength in the periodic superradiance phase. b, Comparison of emission patterns between the many-body case with N = 1010 atoms (blue) and the single-atom case with N = 1 (red). For a fair comparison, the total effective cavity coupling strength is fixed to \({g}_{{\rm{tot}}}=\sqrt{N}g=2\pi \times 1\,{\rm{MHz}}\) for both cases. c, Comparison of emission patterns in the presence (blue) and absence (red) of spin frequency inhomogeneity, i.e., disorder. All simulations are performed using experimental parameters corresponding to the periodic superradiance phase in Regime III.

Recent findings suggest that a and b, show simultaneously recorded microwave periodic superradiance and transferred optical periodic superradiance, respectively, over a duration of up to 100 ms. c, Zoom-in windows near 1, 50, and 100 ms showing synchronized dual-rail emission patterns, maintaining persistent and robust pulse periodicity without decay.

The microwave and optical channels exhibit synchronized and reproducible temporal profiles. The grey shaded area indicates the noise floor determined from the optical signal, below which the phase extraction is not reliable. b, Normalized amplitude stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. τ denotes the peak emission time, identified for each burst from the time-domain pulse train. The microwave and optical pulse trains exhibit synchronized and reproducible phase profiles over time. Phase values in regions dominated by the optical-signal noise floor are greyed out, where large fluctuations are observed. The chirping behaviour during each pulse qualitatively follows the amplitude profile, which can be attributed to an effective Kerr nonlinearity induced intensity dependence. d, Phase stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts, zoomed in on the region above the noise floor. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first 11 games of the Serie A season have produced some rather intriguing trends regarding AC Milan’s attacking productivity.

MilanNews recall how – after the important win in Genoa before the break – Ruben Amorim emphasised how this Milan team are still far from the final product he envisioned in the summer, especially in the final third.

The Rossoneri are improving in possession control and chance creation, but they often remain too far from the opponent’s penalty area for most of the game. This limitation has also affected Gonçalo Ramos, who has been forced to drop deeper, far away from the penalty box.

Industry observers note that after 11 league games, Milan are only 17th in Serie A for shots on goal, averaging 11.5 per game. Yet, they lead Serie A in average xG per shot, at 0.145. In other words, the Rossoneri do not shoot much, but when they do it is very dangerous.

This is also confirmed by the remarkable individual numbers. Adrien Rabiot has scored five goals from 12 shots, with a conversion rate of 41.7%. Diego Moreira is at 40%, Alphadjo Cisse at 38.5%, and Christian Pulisic at 36.4%.

In a recent development, the notable absentee from this ranking is the player expected to score the most: Gonçalo Ramos. The Portuguese has scored just three goals with 33 total shots and 5.35 xG, meaning a conversion rate of 9.1%. These numbers are far from those of his team-mates.

It has been revealed that amorim continues to defend him, emphasising that the problem lies primarily with the team being too deep. Milan must therefore start to generate more territorial dominance, to allow Ramos to operate closer to goal and for him to be on the end of what is clearly quality service being provided.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

His form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

FotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has remarked the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

It has been revealed that his defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

It has been revealed that yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Recent findings suggest that iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

In a recent development, juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

In a recent development, the rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Recent findings suggest that only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

It has been revealed that more key for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

Sources indicate that that leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti mentioned afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

Sources indicate that the count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 days old on Sunday when he finished third in the Mexico City Grand Prix behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.
  • The previous recordholder was Germany's Sebastian Vettel, who first became a world champion at age 23 in 2010.
  • Antonelli is also the first Italian champion since 1953.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 days old on Sunday when he finished third in the Mexico City Grand Prix behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.

The previous recordholder was Germany's Sebastian Vettel, who first became a world champion at age 23 in 2010.

Antonelli is also the first Italian champion since 1953.

"I'm speechless. I’m trying to process what has just happened," noted Antonelli after finishing the race.

His parents and sister were there to embrace him when he stepped out of the car.

He was then mobbed by his pit crew.

In a recent development, "It's been an incredible season, and to share this podium with Max ​and Lewis is truly incredible. And looking forward to some more battles in the future," the 20-year-old said.

Antonelli, who secured the title with four races remaining, mentioned the final lap was complicated by the excitement of what he had achieved.

"I think I lost two seconds because I could not see ahead, I think I saw two Ferraris," he noted. "It was very special, a lot of memories went through my mind at that moment, and I let it all out after achieving one of my biggest dreams.".

Sources indicate that antonelli has now risen to 380 points with four races remaining. Verstappen (261) snuck past Hamilton (259) in the standings, but they will be racing for second the rest of the ​way.

Antonelli started the race in ​fourth and needed to finish ‌ninth or better to secure the championship on Sunday no matter what his peers did.

He had a relatively smooth run, though the race was interrupted by a red flag around Lap ​45 when Valtteri Bottas crashed.

Verstappen, meanwhile, claimed his sixth victory at the Mexico City Grand Prix, further cementing his affinity with the circuit.

After Mexico, F1 will head to Brazil and then to Las Vegas.

The final two Grands Prix are scheduled to be held in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. But it remains uncertain whether they will take place, given the geopolitical instability in the region.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:40, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:42.

Konyaspor will be looking to halt their recent slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Besiktas to Medas Konya Buyuksehir Stadyumu on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with eight points from 11 matches, only outside the bottom three on goal difference, while the Black Eagles occupy fifth place with 19 points from 10 games and will be hoping to maintain their push towards the top of the standings.

Konyaspor have endured a difficult run of results in recent weeks, winning just once in their last six league matches and struggling to find consistency in the final third.

Ilhan Palut's side began that sequence with consecutive goalless draws against Kasimpasa and Istanbul Basaksehir before suffering a 1-0 defeat away to Amed SK.

They then recorded a 2-0 home victory over Genclerbirligi, but that proved to be their only success during the period as they suffered consecutive defeats against Galatasaray (4-0) and Samsunspor (1-0).

Konyaspor were particularly disappointing in their defeat away to Samsunspor just before the break, failing to take anything from a match against a side sitting second-bottom and enduring a losing run.

The result further highlighted their struggles in front of goal, with the hosts having scored just six times in their opening 11 league matches, an average of fewer than one per game, while they have failed to find the net in seven of those fixtures.

Konyaspor have scored four of their six goals and collected seven of their eight points on home soil, although they were thrashed by Galatasaray in their last home game and now face a Besiktas side that have beaten them in their last two league meetings.

The hosts did manage to defeat the Black Eagles 1-0 in their most recent encounter, although that victory came in the Turkish Cup.

Besiktas, meanwhile, have enjoyed a more productive campaign, collecting seven wins, one draw and three defeats from their opening 11 league matches to remain within reach of the leading teams, sitting six points behind league leaders Galatasaray.

Vincenzo Italiano's side are also unbeaten in their last three league games, a sequence that began with a 2-0 home victory over Istanbul Basaksehir before they were held to a 2-2 draw by Kasimpasa.

Their subsequent European fixture saw them suffer a 3-2 defeat against Celtic, but they responded positively three days later by recording a convincing 3-0 home win over Genclerbirligi.

Dusan Vlahovic was particularly influential in that victory, scoring twice as the Black Eagles returned to winning ways in the Super Lig and demonstrated the attacking quality that has made them one of the more productive sides in the division, with only four teams scoring more than their 23 goals.

However, the visitors have struggled on the road, winning just one of their five away league matches and failing to win any of their last three, during which they have recorded one draw and two defeats.

Konyaspor will be without Adil Demirbag, who is recovering from a cruciate ligament injury and is expected to remain sidelined for the rest of the season.

Chidozie Awaziem is also unlikely to feature after sustaining a muscle injury, while Marko Jevtovic is working towards regaining full fitness and faces a late assessment.

Ugurcan Yazgili is another concern after picking up a hamstring problem, leaving Palut with defensive and midfield decisions to make.

Mostafa Mohamed, Diogo Goncalves and Ebrima Colley are among the attacking options available to the Konyaspor manager, although Enis Bardhi is expected to miss out through suspension.

Besiktas will be without Umit Akdag, who is recovering from a broken wrist, while Fabio Miretti is also expected to miss the match with a shoulder injury.

Emmanuel Agbadou is not expected to return until later in December as he continues his recovery from a knee problem, while Orkun Kokcu is also sidelined with a foot injury.

Konyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Gungordu; Andzouana, Baniya, Bosluk, Masuaku; Toth, Ibrahimoglu; Colley, Goncalves, Dompe; Mohamed.

Besiktas possible starting lineup:.

Nubel; Murillo, Taylan Bulut, Topcu, R Yilmaz; Ndidi; Trossard, S Ozcan, Olaitan, Fakili; Vlahovic.

Konyaspor have struggled to produce consistent attacking performances this season, and although Besiktas have been inconsistent on the road, their attacking quality should be enough to overcome the hosts' defensive resistance, with Italiano's side expected to secure a comfortable victory in Konya.

LA communities kick out Big Oil

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Los Angeles has become the largest city in the US to ban oil drilling, after years of lawsuits and campaigning by residents who raised the alarm over pollution and potential health risks from nearby wells .

"Front-line communities have pushed the city for a solution for this for over a decade," remarked local resident Wendy Miranda, who has campaigned for years with STAND-LA, a coalition of community groups working to end neighborhood oil drilling.

The ordinance, approved by the LA City Council on October 28, puts an immediate stop to oil extraction and bans the redrilling or deepening of wells. Existing operations must be phased out within city limits over the next 20 years.

Though LA City is only part of greater Los Angeles, the move affects hundreds of active wells and thousands of inactive ones, many located in working class communities of color.

Industry observers note that "In South LA, working-class families have had corporations drilling across the street from their homes," said council president Marqueece Harris-Dawson in a statement. "No one should have to live near an oil drilling site.".

Rock Zierman, CEO of the California Independent Petroleum Association (CIPA), told DW, "CIPA believes this ordinance constitutes an unlawful taking of private property.".

LA follows much smaller Culver City, also in California, in moving against urban oil production, and begins the process of ending its long, complex relationship with fossil fuels.

Sources indicate that california's oil industry expanded rapidly in the early 20th century, when the state produced roughly a quarter of the world's oil. Lots of that so-called black gold was around LA and as the city grew, homes, schools and businesses were built around existing oil infrastructure.

According to recent reports, today, wells can be found beneath residential areas, close to playgrounds, along the coast and in some of the city's most densely populated and largely working-class neighborhoods. Some have been permanently sealed or plugged for decades, while others remain active or are idle.

Industry observers note that under California law, an idle well is one that has not produced oil for two years. Unlike plugged wells, they can potentially return to production.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Residents living near the active and inactive wells report strong odors, headaches, nausea and breathing difficulties. Another concern is air quality. Oil wells can release toxic pollutants, including benzene and hydrogen sulfide, and research has linked proximity to oil extraction with higher rates of respiratory illness and reduced lung function.

But both active and idle wells can also leak methane — a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change — while residents say occasional accidents or breakages send oil flowing down city streets.

"Frontline communities have been experiencing or have experienced for decades living near these toxic sites and having to pay for that with their health," noted Miranda, a policy director with Esperanza Community Housing, a nonprofit providing affordable housing services.

According to recent reports, miranda told DW she and her mother both have asthma. The council vote "definitely represents hope," she added.

Recent findings suggest that LA City Council initially approved an ordinance to phase out oil extraction back in 2022 after successful lobbying by residents like Wendy Miranda. But oil companies challenged the measure in court, with industry groups successfully arguing that the city lacked the legal authority to impose the ban.

California subsequently passed legislation giving local governments greater power to regulate and restrict oil and gas operations, putting the possibility of a phaseout back on the table.

In an emailed statement to DW, CIPA CEO Rock Zierman said energy companies were prepared to challenge the new ordinance.

Zierman added that it would make city residents more dependent on foreign oil from countries with lower environmental standards when they are "already struggling" with high gas prices.

"It sends the jobs, investment and revenue elsewhere while leaving Californians to pay the bill," said Zierman.

It has been revealed that the relationship between local oil production and prices at the pump is not straightforward and is influenced by a number of factors, according to the California Energy Commission, the state's main energy policy agency. Those include the cost of crude oil, refining, transportation, distribution and local taxes.

In a recent development, even though the US is the world's largest oil producer, it exports and imports crude oil, as well as refined petroleum products. Because oil is traded globally, US residents are exposed to the same price fluctuations as people elsewhere, no matter how much of the fossil fuel is produced domestically.

Sources indicate that california's oil industry and the amount of oil it produces have been steadily declining since the 1980s. In the coastal lowlands known as the LA Basin, output is 43% lower than eight years ago, with the amount of oil extracted falling more rapidly than the number of open wells.

In a recent development, when wells stop producing, it is up to the oil operators to remove equipment and plug them. The state agency that regulates oil and gas, CalGEM, and the LA fire department oversee plugging operations, and also seal wells for which no-one takes responsibility.

But many have not yet been plugged — some 80% of idle wells in LA have been inactive for more than eight years, and about a third for over a century.

The cost of plugging a well also varies widely, with estimates ranging from hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars. California law requires operators to submit plugging plans or face annual fines that increase with the amount of time the well has been idle.

But those fines aren't always paid. According to CalGEM's own data, the agency collected just $1 million out of $36 million (€32 million) in fines in 2025.

A report by Carbon Tracker also found that if all future profits from oil companies operating in California went to decommissioning wells, the state would still face a shortfall of $7 billion. The cost would by default fall to taxpayers, according to Carbon Tracker.

Miranda told DW that the next step for community activists is to reduce the 20-year timeline and have the oil sector "pay for this cleanup."  For now, she is indicates both she and her mother are hopeful that future generations "can have better health and breathe cleaner air.".

Published: 14:59 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 18 November 2026.

Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.

Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.

The 40-year-old, who suffered a dislocated shoulder in the fall, underwent tests in hospital which determined that a 'meningeal irritation' had been the cause of his collapse.

Sources indicate that if left untreated meningeal irritation can become meningitis. The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.

Kompany was discharged from hospital the following week to continue his recovery at home.

The Belgian coach is now set to return to the dugout when Bayern face Cologne on Friday, with Kompany due to also address the media tomorrow morning.

Vincent Kompany is set to return to the Bayern Munich dugout for their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Kompany's return was officially confirmed by Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen.

'Yes, Vincent is in pretty good spirits. I ran into him today,' Dreesen told German outlet Abendzeitung.

Recent findings suggest that 'The meningeal irritation has healed. He has already undergone shoulder surgery.'.

Kompany had led training for the first time since his collapse earlier this week, with his arm reportedly in a sling following his shoulder injury.

He had missed five matches during his recovery with Bayern winning two and drawing against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

The German champions also beat Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in his absence, as well as progressing in the DFB Cup.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks had overseen the first team during his recovery.

Danks previously worked as Kompany's assistant at Anderlecht before deputising for Dean Smith and Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa and Michael Carrick at Middlesbrough.

Kompany has missed five matches following his collapse at Bayern's training ground on October 23.

Bayern had stressed they wanted to give Kompany as much time as required to recover before returning to work.

The German giants play eight matches in the next month, including two matches in the Champions League, before the Bundesliga takes its winter break.

Reports had emerged after Kompany's collapse that club officials had been concerned by his irregular eating habits, as well as barely exercising, drinking excessive amounts of coffee, and taking on too much work.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl dismissed the claims last month, reiterating that Kompany's illness had been the cause of his collapse rather than his workload.

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 22:07.

Trabzonspor will look to extend their winning run in the league to seven games when they host bottom-placed Eyupspor at Papara Park on Sunday.

The Black Sea outfit sit second in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 25 points from 11 matches, three behind league leaders Galatasaray, while the visitors are 18th with just three points, five adrift of safety.

Thomas Reis has made an excellent start to his reign, winning all six of his league games in charge, with the latest victory coming in a 2-0 away triumph over Alanyaspor just before the international break, as Wagner Pina opened the scoring in the 17th minute before Muhammed Salah doubled their advantage in the 34th.

That result represented a strong response to their 1-0 defeat to Freiburg in the Conference League, which brought an end to their seven-game winning streak across all competitions.

Trabzonspor will now look to begin another run of victories, and their attacking and defensive records suggest they have every reason to be confident, having scored 26 goals, the fourth-highest tally in the division, while conceding just eight, the fewest in the league, as they build a strong foundation in their pursuit of a first league title since 2021-22.

The hosts have also won all five of their league games at home this season, and another victory would see them match the club's best start to a home league campaign, last achieved in 1984-85.

Meanwhile, Eyupspor are in deep trouble after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Kocaelispor last time out, their eighth consecutive league loss and the ninth time in 11 matches this season that they have failed to score in the division.

No other side has conceded more goals than Eyupspor this season, with their tally standing at 30, while they have also scored just three times, the fewest in the league.

Mustafa Dalci said after the defeat to Kocaelispor that his side are entering a period in which they must start collecting points, but their prospects look bleak ahead of another difficult away fixture, particularly as they have conceded a league-high 19 goals on their travels.

Their head-to-head record against Trabzonspor offers little encouragement either, with Eyupspor yet to win any of their four previous meetings, drawing one and losing three, while they have failed to score in all four encounters.

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 22:07.

BB Erzurumspor will be looking to end their recent losing run when they welcome Goztepe to Kazim Karabekir Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 12th in the Turkish Super Lig standings after 11 matches, while the visitors occupy 10th place and will be hoping to bounce back from their latest defeat to maintain their push towards the upper half of the table.

Erzurumspor had enjoyed an encouraging spell before their recent setbacks, recording victories over Eyupspor and Gaziantep, as well as a draw with Alanyaspor and a win against Samsunspor, to put together a four-game unbeaten run and move away from the lower reaches of the standings.

However, their momentum was checked when they suffered a 3-1 home defeat against Corum before losing 2-1 away to Caykur Rizespor in their most recent league outing before the international break.

Erzurumspor took the lead against Rizespor through Ibrahim Diabate, but they were unable to hold on to their advantage as the hosts turned the contest around, leaving Serkan Ozbalta's side with consecutive defeats after they had collected 10 points from their preceding four matches.

Despite those setbacks, the hosts will be encouraged by their home performances this season, having beaten Konyaspor, Eyupspor and Samsunspor while suffering defeats against Galatasaray and Corum, the latter being their most recent appearance in front of their supporters.

They will be keen to rediscover the defensive organisation that helped them secure those three victories without conceding, particularly against a Goztepe side that has demonstrated considerable attacking quality in recent weeks.

This will be the fifth Super Lig meeting between the sides, with Erzurumspor picking up two wins, drawing one and losing one of the previous four, although they have lost their last two encounters against the visitors, one in the Turkish Cup and the other in the second division.

Goztepe, meanwhile, had been enjoying an impressive run of results before their latest setback, winning four consecutive league matches as part of a six-game unbeaten streak to establish themselves in the top half of the table.

Stanimir Stoilov's side began that sequence with a 4-0 away victory over Eyupspor before recording a 2-1 win against Kocaelispor and a 2-0 home triumph over Corum.

The visitors then produced one of their most impressive performances of the campaign by defeating Fenerbahce 2-1 away from home.

However, their winning streak came to an end just before the break when they suffered a 2-1 home defeat against Istanbul Basaksehir, with Juan finding the net but the hosts ultimately unable to prevent their opponents from taking all three points.

Goztepe nevertheless have an away unbeaten run to protect, with Goz Goz having gone four games without defeat on the road, winning their last three and drawing the other.

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (966 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The president of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Franz Reindl, announced shortly after the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Friday, that he had called a meeting of its main decision-making body for Monday and Tuesday.
  • In a recent development, the Lausanne-based court had ruled that the IIHF must allow Russian national teams to take part in ice hockey world championships again.
  • "Our task now is to implement this ruling responsibly," said Germany's Reindl, who was elected IIHF president just last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The president of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Franz Reindl, announced shortly after the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Friday, that he had called a meeting of its main decision-making body for Monday and Tuesday.

In a recent development, the Lausanne-based court had ruled that the IIHF must allow Russian national teams to take part in ice hockey world championships again. They had been barred from doing so since shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

"Our task now is to implement this ruling responsibly," said Germany's Reindl, who was elected IIHF president just last month.

It has been revealed that "Several championships are only weeks away, and changes to participation affect many people; players, teams, organizing committees and host cities," he remarked. "We will work closely with all of them to find practical solutions.".

Sources indicate that the first tournament the CAS decision applies to is the World Juniors, to be held beginning on December 26 in Canada. Just how it will affect the tournament is not clear. Hockey Canada mentioned it was in contact with the IIHF and had briefed Prime Minister Mark Carney's government on the decision.

Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand told public broadcaster CBC that she is "not comfortable" with allowing a Russian team to take part in the tournament in Alberta.

It has been revealed that "This is a very unwelcome decision given the geopolitical situation, given the actions of Russia," she said. "All options are on the table, and I will say, again, I greet this decision with great disappointment.".

Canada's secretary of state for sport, Adam van Koeverden, appeared to rule out Russian athletes being granted visas for the tournament.

"Canada will maintain restrictions on the participation of Russian athletes at events hosted in Canada that receive funding from the Government of Canada and explore further options to ensure that the Russian government is held accountable," he mentioned in a statement.

Germany is also considering its options as it prepares to host the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Düsseldorf and Mannheim in May.

"The German government takes a very critical view of the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport, a government spokesman said on Sunday, according to the DPA news agency.

"The German government will discuss possible consequences of the ruling, including for the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany, with the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) promptly.".

The DEB's chief executive, Frank Lutz, is to travel to Berlin to discuss the matter with government officials this week. Speaking on broadcaster MagentaSport on the weekend, he conceded that surrendering Germany's hosting rights for the lucrative tournament was a possibility.

Industry observers note that "I do not want to paint a black picture. I do not want to call the World Championship into question either. But of course, we at the DEB also have to consider the option of handing back this championship," he said.

Several other national ice hockey federations have expressed disappointment at the CAS decision, including those of Ukraine, Sweden, Finland, and Czechia.

The International Olympic Committee opened the door for Russian athletes to return to international competition when it lifted its ban of the Russian Olympic Committee in July. However, the IIHF had already decided to continue to exclude Russian teams for the 2026-27 season – over security concerns. The CAS decision – handed down after an appeal by Russia – found this reasoning was insufficiently proven.

The Kremlin's reaction to the ruling was, unsurprisingly, positive.

"Russia is returning to world hockey. This place rightfully belongs to us, and discrimination in hockey has been brought to an end," Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev told state television channel Vesti.

A boycott of the World Juniors, Men's World Championships or other tournaments by individual nations is now emerging as a real possibility.

"We are presently working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen remarked in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday evening.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

By Tuesday afternoon, the Finland-led effort was gaining steam, with Sweden, Norway and Denmark making similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson said in a statement.

This came shortly after Norway noted it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

"Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors tournament.

There has been the suggestion, that having won this victory at the CAS, Russia's next focus could be on football, where its national and club teams remain excluded from international competitions.

Russian FA general secretary Maxim Mitrofanov told state news agency Tass that there "should be one rule for all.".

World football's governing body FIFA allowed a Russia boys' team to play under its national flag in the inaugural Under-15 World Cup and Festival in Azerbaijan, which kicked off last week and ends on Saturday.

In a recent development, this article was originally published on November 2, 2026. It was updated on November 3 with the statement from the Finnish Ice Hockey Association. It was later updated with the statements from the Swedish, Norwegian and Danish federations.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.

Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s upcoming home or at least they will when everything is in order.

Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.

From wherever it ends up, it will project a moment in time when everything changed for Tyler, having walked away from a steady job at ITV and taken a leap of faith as lead commentator for the fresh satellite channel.

'A fresh frontier,' admits Tyler, the undisputed ‘Voice of the Premier League’ by the time he left the role at Sky, more than 30 years later.

Sources indicate that 'We didn’t know where it would take us, so that was a special day. Feeling a bit like a pioneer. Wondering whether we were all on a fool’s errand. Some people turned down the job I accepted because of the risk. My kids were four and two at the time.

'We used to travel to the games by train in those days, and we would look out of the window and count the satellite dishes as we passed through a substantial town. We didn’t know whether it was going to work. I wasn’t sure anybody would be watching.

Legendary football commentator Martin Tyler has released a book: TALES FROM THE GANTRY.

Tyler was the undoubted 'Voice of the Premier League' by the time he left Sky Sports in 2023.

Sources indicate that 'It was slow off the ground and there was a feeling within the game against live football, that people wouldn’t go to the games if they were televised live, and it ended up the opposite. Attendances have gone up, an amazing paradox. Now you can’t get a ticket.'.

Televised football has come a long way since Tyler’s first commentary game, Southampton v Sheffield Wednesday in the old Division Two in 1974, shot with just four cameras for Southern Television.

'Now if you don’t have 24 cameras you can feel a bit short-changed,' he laughs. 'I worked at ITV for about 17 years, most of it commentating and you would get a crew on match day who had been doing Coronation Street or Emmerdale Farm in the week and a match director from light entertainment.'.

Recent findings suggest that the Premier League has come a long way, too. Some might argue too far. It has led football from its roots as the working man’s game to a place where clubs are owned by nations states and mired in the legal complications of the Manchester City case.

Tyler wants to reserve comment on City’s financial offences until sentencing is passed, aware he is inextricably bound to their success because of his iconic commentary for Sergio Aguero’s winner in the 93rd minute against Queen’s Park Rangers to snatch the Premier League title from Manchester United in 2012.

'I’ve always stated you won’t see anything like it again, and I stick to that,' he notes, although he the 'Aguero moment’ as it has become commonly known probably means less to him than it does to others.

He is proud to deliver the words but insists those moments belong to the players, the clubs and the fans, not to him.

Ask about his favourite game from three decades in the Premier League and Tyler instinctively pulls Liverpool’s 4-3 comeback win against Newcastle in 1996 from the thrillers he has called.

His own footballing background, meanwhile, could hardly be any further from the Premier League’s glitzy, moneyed elite.

Sources indicate that tyler has always supported Woking and played as an amateur for Corinthian-Casuals. 'The law was you couldn’t get paid,' he says. 'We were on expenses only and they weren’t dodgy expenses. If I went on the tube to Leytonstone, I got the tube fare repaid and no more.

'I played for five years at that level and never got a penny because that was the rule. I played my last game in 1973 and within two years’ they got rid of it because so many people were bending the rules. An opposition player told me their team were on £75 a game.'.

Tyler reflected on his time in the game as a player, coach and commentator with Daily Mail Sport's Matt Barlow.

He was famously on commentary for Sergio Aguero's title-winning moment in 2012.

From a cricketing family, Tyler was on the books at Surrey where he twice served as 12th man and lived for a time with Bob Willis, who became one of England’s greatest fast bowlers after moving on to Warwickshire.

His manager for a time at Casuals was Surrey legend Micky Stewart, who had also played for the famous amateur football club before turning professional at Charlton. In those days it was possible for the multi-talented to hold down a decent career in two sports.

An afternoon in Tyler’s company is just as likely to involve digressions into non-league football, where he worked as an assistant to Alan Dowson at clubs including Woking and Hampton & Richmond, as it is into the Premier League.

He might regale you with a story about Arsene Wenger and the time, on the way to the gantry at Wigan Athletic, he slipped deeper than he realised into long conversation with the then Arsenal boss about rioting in Paris and almost missed his pre-match slot.

And he might pivot from there into Wenger’s fierce rivalry with Sir Alex Ferguson. 'I have seen Arsene very, very grumpy,' says Tyler. 'When he lost the FA Cup semi-final when Dennis Bergkamp missed the penalty and Ryan Giggs scored.

'I have never seen a manager so angry because he knew he had handed over not only an FA Cup final place but also the domination they enjoyed at that time. They had done the Double in 98 and he felt that was not only about losing a match but losing their psychological edge over their greatest rivals. He was livid. Talk about winning and losing with dignity.'.

But there’s every chance he will reminisce about the time when, as a schoolboy Woking supporter in the terrible winter of 1962-63 he was rewarded for volunteering to paint the stands with an invitation to travel on the team bus to an Amateur Cup tie at Lydbrook Athletic.

Industry observers note that 'We left Woking at seven on the morning of the match for a two o’clock kick-off in Gloucestershire and by nine we were digging the bus out of a snowdrift on the A4,' says Tyler. 'We got there at four, no floodlights, and they had marked the lines on the snow with blue soap powder but there was no way we could play. We turned around to go back, got stuck in Cheltenham and had to stay for the night.'.

The only other footballing image on display in Tyler’s home is a photograph of him and Dowson celebrating as the final whistle confirmed their Hampton & Richmond side as Isthmian League champions in 2016.

Tyler has had a hugely varied career, all the way from grassroots level right to the top.

Tyler even worked as an assistant coach to Alan Dowson at several Non-League clubs.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

After collecting the trophy, Tyler jumped into his car, drove north and less than 24 hours later was at the King Power Stadium to see Leicester crowned champions of England.

'The greatest fairytale story in the Premier League,' as he says. 'I had sampled that in a tiny non-league way, then taken those feelings with me to Leicester where it was multiplied a million times, but I could tell the world a tiny bit about how wonderful they must be feeling.'.

The range of his experience is vast. From amateur football in the 60s, through regional television and ITV to Sky’s Premier League revolution. He commentates regularly and coaches at Woking’s academy and has written a book.

Industry observers note that it is a wonderful compilation of 110 essays, the reflections on his lifetime in football. 'The random thoughts of a football obsessive,' as he likes to call it.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino.
  • Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches.
  • Sources indicate that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

Sources indicate that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the fresh refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

Sources indicate that the wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

Recent findings suggest that the trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

Recent findings suggest that the contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

It has been revealed that luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Industry observers note that close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

In a recent development, the run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

According to recent reports, the first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

One of the interesting subplots to this evening’s game will be watching Johan Manzambi playing for Aston Villa.

The Switzerland international’s decision to reject Newcastle in order to sign for Villa helped convince Eddie Howe to quit in the summer.

Having already missed out on Victor Munoz, who decided to join Liverpool at the last moment, losing Manzambi - their first-choice target across the position board - was a blow Howe did not feel he could recover from.

In short, he was not convinced the alternatives would give him the tools to do the job this season. Aladji Bamba, who was signed instead, has not started a game for Newcastle this season and appears to be well down the pecking order in the centre midfield under Howe’s successor Matthias Jaissle.

Manzambi had a slow start to his Villa career because of injury but he was hugely impressive at the World Cup for Switzerland and is expected to become one of the best midfield players in Europe over the next few years. Nobody can say with any degree of confidence that will be the same for Bamba.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 22:35, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 01:26.

Fulham goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with an Achilles injury.

The Frenchman sustained the injury in a behind-closed-doors game against West Ham United during the international break.

Revealing the extent of the injury, Alvaro Arbeloa told reporters on Friday: "Unfortunately, Lecomte injured his Achilles tendon against West Ham, so he will be out for the rest of the season.

“We are sorry for him because he is very important and it was very sad.”.

Lecomte has not played in the Premier League this season, but he featured in three of Fulham’s EFL Cup games, including a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace last month.

As a result of Lecomte’s injury, Alex Borto and Dino Kaiser will be the backup options for the club’s undisputed first-choice goalkeeper Bernd Leno.

Arbeloa also revealed Emile Smith Rowe is unlikely to be fit for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off against Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium.

“Smith Rowe has some pain in his hip, so I think he won't be available for tomorrow.

“I think it’s nothing serious - some pain and discomfort, so we will see next week, but it doesn't look really serious.”.

The news of Smith Rowe's physical glitch represents the latest setback in what is proving to be a difficult campaign for the Arsenal academy product.

The 28-year-old made 37 Premier League appearances in Marco Silva's final season in charge, but he has featured in just four league games under Arbeloa due to injury and selection decisions.

In more positive news, Arbeloa explained that Tom Cairney could be in contention to return to the squad after missing the draw against Newcastle United before the international window.

If available, Cairney could have a role to play off the bench as Fulham look to end their woeful run of form against Manchester City.

The Cottagers have lost each of their last 17 Premier League games against the Citizens since they played out a 2-2 draw at Craven Cottage in September 2011.

Meanwhile, their last head-to-head victory took place in April 2009 when Clinton Dempsey netted a brace in a 3-1 win at the Etihad Stadium.

When building a squad it is crucial to have a vision of the end goal, and AC Milan have exactly that heading into 2027.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by stating that there are no transition years when it comes to Milan. Frequently they have chosen to overhaul the squad in the summer window, and sometimes even in the winter.

It has been revealed that for example, 2024 brought Paulo Fonseca with Morata, Pavlovic, Fofana, Emerson Royal, Jimenez and Abraham. Then, 2025 brought Gimenez, then Massimiliano Allegri with Modric, Rabiot, Nkunku, Jashari, and De Winter. Last summer brought Ruben Amorim with Ramos, Moreira, Gila, and Cisse.

Recent findings suggest that A not-so-bold prediction: 2027 won’t be slow. Gerry Cardinale even hinted at this, stating: “We’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic. It will take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.” The two transfer windows? Winter and summer, 2027.

The Rossoneri have two key needs right now: a striker and a central defender. They’ll try to secure them as early as the month after next. Nicolo Tresoldi and Endrick are the names that have been talked about for weeks, but the transfer market has surprises.

According to recent reports, the difficulties are well known: Club Brugge do not want to sell their jewel in January unless a €60m check materialises, while with Endrick it seems the will of Jose Mourinho must be taken into account. So, alternative names could emerge for the attack.

A central defender is less of a pressing need. Eight months ago, Milan decided to explore the possibility of signing Virgil van Dijk, who turned 35 in July and is regarded as one of the best of his generation.

A year ago, the conditions weren’t there, but now they might be. Van Dijk’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by Milan and Italy. It’s complex, but it’s worth a try, and Cardinale seems to agree.

Then there is Gabriele Calvani. He’s Italian, 22, plays for Frosinone, and is expected to start San Siro on Sunday. The Diavolo are interested, just as they are keen on Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio, whom Amorim has already coached and attempted to sign in the summer.

Industry observers note that milan will undoubtedly make some changes to their bench over the next 12 months, aiming to mix young players with experienced players. Filippo Terracciano will leave in January, Vladimirov needs to play, Hutchinson is on loan until June, and Jashari will have to reconsider his future.

In a recent development, it’s certain that some Diawara-like players will arrive, i.e. promising prospects chosen through scouting and data. Markus Krösche – if he becomes the upcoming Head of Football, as is now almost certain – will have extensive powers in this regard.

Recent findings suggest that the idea of ​​making the team more Italian is there, but we know how the market works, making it difficult to plan. Not only that, but some Italians will soon leave Milan too. Above all, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda are heading out on loan.

It has been revealed that the former seems destined for Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, while it remains to be seen where and under what terms the altter will leave. A loan with an option to buy, leaving Milan free to control the future, probably. To a small Serie A team? Possibly, but a move abroad is possible too.

Belgium and the Netherlands are countries where strikers historically have more opportunities in teams that are younger, while Germany could be another destination. If he takes a flight north, don’t be surprised.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder highlights near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate–forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

Sources indicate that symbols indicate data sources, including sites with (1) both eddy-covariance flux and phenocam observations (n = 3; green stars); (2) eddy-covariance flux only (n = 1; blue star); (3) phenocam observations only (n = 2; yellow stars); (4) litterfall observations (n = 47; red triangles); (5) inventory plots (n = 289; purple circles); and (6) very high-resolution Google Earth image locations (n = 16; 0.5-m spatial resolution, each covering a 2 km × 2 km area; blue squares). Site information, including location, data type, and observation period, is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The map was created using ArcGIS Pro with the Esri World Ocean Base basemap. Basemap sources: Esri, Garmin, GEBCO, NOAA NGDC and other contributors.

Industry observers note that panels a-e compare the temporal dynamics of ecosystem-scale deciduousness fraction from Sentinel-2 (blue line) with the fraction of leafless tree crowns visually assessed from phenocam images (black line). The Sentinel-2 deciduousness fraction is calculated as the mean value within a 500 m × 500 m area centred on each phenocam site, while the phenocam typically covers an area of approximately 100 m × 100 m. Panel f reveals the relationship between Sentinel-2-derived deciduousness and the corresponding deciduousness derived from phenocam observations across five sites (n = 60 paired site-month observations). The solid line indicates an ordinary least-squares linear regression, with statistical significance assessed using a two-sided test (p = 6.17 × 10−22).

In a recent development, a, Relationship between standardized monthly litterfall and standardized satellite-derived deciduousness across annual cycles at 47 Amazonian sites (n = 559 pooled site-month observations). The red line indicates the ordinary least-squares linear regression across all pooled data, and the inset boxplot summarizes the site-level distribution of correlation coefficients (r, n = 47 sites). b, Relationship between satellite-derived deciduousness amplitude and the ground-derived proportion of deciduous tree species across the Amazon basin. Grey circles represent raw plot-to-pixel observations (n = 289 plots). The red line shows the ordinary least-squares linear fit to the raw observations, and the shaded band indicates the 95% confidence interval of the fitted mean relationship. The dashed grey line indicates the 1:1 relationship. For a and b, statistical significance of the regression slopes was assessed using two-sided tests (a, p = 2.52 × 10−141; b, p = 7.24 × 10−28). The p values were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. c, Patch-level comparison of deciduousness derived from Sentinel-2 (y-axis) against that derived from closely date-matched, high-resolution Google Earth imagery (GEI; x-axis) via image-specific Random Forest classification and pooled across all 16 validation scenes. Each dot represents a 100-m × 100-m aggregated patch (n = 6058 patches), and the dashed black line marks the 1:1 relationship. d, e, Scene-level distributions of correlation coefficients (r; d) and root-mean-square errors (RMSE; e) calculated separately for each of the 16 GEI validation scenes. Grey dots represent individual scenes. In all boxplots, the centre line indicates the median, the box bounds the interquartile range (IQR), and the whiskers extend to 1.5 × IQR.

Industry observers note that a, c, e, g, Spatial maps of evergreen forest cover (a), MODIS Vegetation Continuous Fields tree cover (c), EVI amplitude (e) and VOD amplitude (g). Positive values indicate improved seasonal agreement with SIF after incorporating leaf-age-dependent physiological dynamics, whereas negative values indicate reduced agreement. #48835. Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?

Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (867 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With more than $1 trillion (€900 billion) pouring into the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout, US tech giants are now competing with governments and companies in Europe for the same investment capital.
  • In a recent development, four of the Massive Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google owner Alphabet, Meta and Oracle — have issued about $250 billion in bonds in dollars since the beginning of 2025, according to a tally of filings to US financial regulators by AI Industry Reviews, an independent platform that evaluates AI tools.
  • Recently, Microsoft, the last of the Big Five to hold back, joined the AI borrowing spree with a $25 billion bond sale, all in dollars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With more than $1 trillion (€900 billion) pouring into the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout, US tech giants are now competing with governments and companies in Europe for the same investment capital.

In a recent development, four of the Massive Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google owner Alphabet, Meta and Oracle — have issued about $250 billion in bonds in dollars since the beginning of 2025, according to a tally of filings to US financial regulators by AI Industry Reviews, an independent platform that evaluates AI tools. They have sold a further €37 billion ($41 billion) of bonds in euros.

Recently, Microsoft, the last of the Big Five to hold back, joined the AI borrowing spree with a $25 billion bond sale, all in dollars.

According to recent reports, next year, Goldman Sachs projects that total newly introduced AI hyperscaler bond sales are expected to reach $420 billion. About €60 billion will be issued in euros, according to Dutch bank ING.

That is unwelcome news for European companies and countries like France, Germany and Italy, whose sovereign bond yields have risen sharply in recent months and are already straining public finances.

With public debt at 119% of gross domestic product (GDP) and a deficit still running above 5%, France is already paying a sizable risk premium on its debt. Over the past six months, yields on French 10-year bonds have climbed from roughly 3.7% to nearly 5%.

The French government's interest bill is set to rise from €79 billion currently to €91 billion next year and over €100 billion by 2028.

Based on these figures alone, France's Finance Ministry needs to find tens of billions of euros in additional cuts, tax hikes, or more borrowing by the end of the decade.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In August, economists at the European Central Bank said the euro bond market was adapting well to the presence of AI giants but warned they "could make it harder for other companies and other economic sectors to access finance.".

Writing in a blog post, they also questioned whether the bloc's financial markets can "smoothly handle such large and concentrated debt inflows and warned of a "potential spillover to the sovereign and supranational segment of the bond market.".

That means governments and international lenders such as the European Union and the European Investment Bank could also end up paying more to borrow.

Viktor Hjort, global head of credit strategy at the French bank BNP Paribas, described the phenomenon as "bond abundance.".

Hjort told DW that the presence of the hyperscalers in the euro bond market is "already high enough to create competition" within the corporate sector and "between corporates and governments for available fixed income funds." These are investment funds that mostly buy bonds, which pay regular interest.

Bond yields jumped again last month, driven by rebounding energy prices linked to the Iran war and France’s political crisis, which Hjort noted further revealed the growing competition for capital, as government and manufacturer borrowing costs rose together.

Normally, nervous investors move into government bonds during uncertain times, which pushes their borrowing costs down.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that goldman Sachs warned last week that rising interest costs were starting to hurt earnings at European companies. Among firms in the Stoxx 600 — an index of 600 large, mid-sized and small companies across Europe — Goldman found that interest costs as a share of sales have risen by nearly half since 2022.

The bank's analysts mentioned this had cut earnings by more than 5% over the same period.

Factor in the competition from AI bonds, and European firms could now face pressure to cut their investments in newly introduced plants, equipment and research, as well as shareholder payouts, to prioritize loan repayments.

It has been revealed that the pressure doesn't stop at national governments. Europe's cities and regions, whose borrowing helps to fund schools, transport and infrastructure, may also feel the effects of the AI boom.

Sources indicate that A study for the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development(OECD), published in January, compared local bond markets in Belgium, Germany, Spain, Sweden and Canada. Where AI was spreading fastest, measured by the share of AI-related job vacancies, borrowing costs for cities and regions tended to rise.

"Whereas in the United States, my research has found that AI investments are linked to a lower cost of borrowing for municipalities, the opposite appears to hold in several European countries," the study's co-author, Christos Makridis of Arizona State University's W. P. Carey School of Business, told DW.

While AI bonds are far from the sole cause of Europe's widening fiscal strains, US Massive Tech's huge appetite for capital could add further pressure next year, due to the additional billions in new bonds planned.

The irony is that European taxpayers could end up paying more on their own governments' debt, partly to help finance an AI boom across the Atlantic.

#48833. Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies: Who has won more honours?
